newsitem.title: UK: ENGLISH SPORTS COUNCIL HANDS OUT NEARLY NINE MILLION POUNDS.
newsitem.headline: ENGLISH SPORTS COUNCIL HANDS OUT NEARLY NINE MILLION POUNDS.

text.p: The English Sports Council handed out nearly nine million pounds sterling ($14.8 million) in National Lottery money to seven sports federations on Tuesday.

Athletics has been awarded the major share of the cash with 2.6 million pounds ($4.2 million) in the coming year, including $1.7 million ($2.7 million) to be distributed among 195 athletes for living and training costs.
The Amateur Swimming Association is the next biggest beneficiary with two million pounds ($3.2 million).

Major sports bodies were invited to apply to the Council for Lottery funds last January by producing a long-term performance plan detailing their aims and objectives. The money allotted on Monday is for the first year of their performance plans only.
Announcing the awards, Trevor Brooking, chairman of the Lottery Awards Panel and a former England footballer, said Britain was entering a new era for sport.
"It's a level of funding that British sports has never experienced before," Brooking said.
Sports Minister Tony Banks said sport was important for the whole country.
"There's something about sport and its effect on the psychology of the nation," Banks said. "When we are going well everyone feels good.
"If we are looking for the feel-good factor, as politicians do, this is one way we can get the feel-good factor."
British Athletic Federation (BAF) chief coach Malcolm Arnold welcomed the money and said the federation would now appoint four head coaches.
International rowing manager David Tanner said the federation was happy with its allotment of nearly 1.9 million pounds ($3 million) which he said would encourage young talent to stay in the sport.
"We are talking about the future in the new millennium, not in the next two to three years," Tanner said.

Steve Redgrave and Matthew Pinsent won Britain's only gold medal at last year's Atlanta Olympics with victory in the coxless pairs. It was Britain's poorest Olympic performance since the 1952 Helsinki Games.
